Paper and pencil and minimal human augmentation from software looks like this: Say an airport can take 15 planes in a 15 minute window. "Well, the airlines will schedule 32." He says he's handing the airlines that data and asking them to spread out.

events.raw_text: Do you do all your prompting on Ultrafast? I do. That's sick. Yeah. That's crazy. You know, seven people's dots can, working together, create something new that kind of existed in all of our heads to some degree, but was like an emergent thing. Hey, this is Dan Shipper. You might be wondering what happened to AI and I. This is the same show, we are just rebranding it to the Every Podcast. I'm really excited for our first episode with Sam Waltman. Here it is. Sam, welcome to the show. Thanks for having me. Psyched to have you here. So we're here at Dev Day. I think if you had told me four years ago that the coding models were at this level of capability, I would have been like, wow, I don't know if there would be a lot of developers at Dev Day. but there's more developers than ever, it seems like, and more work to do than ever. So what has the, like, riding the increasing capabilities of coding models and seeing the impact on engineering taught you about the future of engineering and more broadly, like, the future of work with AI? I think people just want so much more stuff. People's expectations are so high. And I think that's a wonderful thing. I think this is why we'll all have this incredible future in front of us to explore. But developers, they've never been able to do more, but there's never been a higher bar either. And I think that's great. I think that's like a nice thing about society. Is that something that surprised you? Did you expect that to happen? I think I was never as doomery about the job stuff as other people, but it still has surprised me somewhat on the upside of just how much latent demand existed in the world and also how much people have remained at the center of everything that is happening with AI. Do you think there's a limit to that, or do you think that translates pretty cleanly to other areas of work? I think there will be some areas of work where there's actually not much creativity required and we don't care about the person doing it. And many of those tasks or jobs will be done by AI.
